name: Order events by likelihood
description: Student can order everyday events from least to most likely.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders three events from least likely to most likely.
commonError: Student orders by preference rather than likelihood.
checkpointTask: Give several events. Ask the student to order them by likelihood.

name: Compare likelihood from proportions
description: Student can compare the likelihood of an outcome based on proportions.
exampleOfSuccess: From bags with different numbers of red balls, the student says which is more likely to give red.
commonError: Student compares total balls rather than the proportion of red.
checkpointTask: Show bags with different proportions. Ask the student which is more likely to give a colour.

name: Identify an independent event
description: Student can identify an event whose outcome does not depend on previous ones.
exampleOfSuccess: After 5 heads, the student says the next toss is still equally likely heads or tails.
commonError: Student thinks past results change the next independent outcome.
checkpointTask: Pose repeated independent events. Ask the student whether past results change the next.

name: Identify a dependent event
description: Student can identify an event whose outcome depends on a previous one.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says drawing a second card without replacing the first changes the chances.
commonError: Student treats a dependent event as if it were independent.
checkpointTask: Pose with-and-without replacement situations. Ask the student which outcomes depend on earlier ones.

name: Identify possible outcomes of an experiment
description: Student can identify the possible outcomes of a chance experiment.
exampleOfSuccess: For tossing two coins, the student lists head-head, head-tail, tail-head, tail-tail.
commonError: Student misses an outcome, or lists impossible ones.
checkpointTask: Name chance experiments. Ask the student to list the possible outcomes.

name: Conduct repeated trials and record
description: Student can conduct repeated trials and record the results.
exampleOfSuccess: The student tosses two coins many times and tallies each outcome.
commonError: Student stops early or does not record every trial.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to run repeated trials and record the results.

name: Describe variation in results
description: Student can describe the variation in results across repeated trials.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notes head-tail came up more often than two heads, and that runs differ.
commonError: Student expects every outcome to be equally frequent.
checkpointTask: After trials, ask the student to describe how the results varied.

name: Relate results to expected outcomes
description: Student can relate the observed results to what they expected.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says two heads happened less than expected this time, but more trials would even out.
commonError: Student treats a short run as the true chance.
checkpointTask: After trials, ask the student to compare their results to what they expected.
